title: Knowledge Localization in Mixture-of-Experts LLMs Using Cross-Lingual Inconsistency
abstract: arXiv:2603.17102v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Modern LLMs continue to exhibit significant variance in behavior across languages, such as being able to recall factual information in some languages but not others. While typically studied as a problem to be mitigated, in this work, we propose leveraging this cross-lingual inconsistency as a tool for interpretability in mixture-of-experts (MoE) LLMs. Our knowledge localization framework contrasts routing for sets of languages where the model correctly recalls information from languages where it fails. This allows us to isolate model components that play a functional role in answering about a piece of knowledge. Our method proceeds in two stages: (1) querying the model with difficult factual questions across a diverse set of languages to generate "success" and "failure" activation buckets and then (2) applying a statistical contrastive analysis to the MoE router logits to identify experts important for knowledge. translated_title: 利用跨语言不一致性在混合专家大语言模型中进行知识定位
translated_abstract: 现代大语言模型在不同语言之间的行为表现出显著差异，例如能够在某些语言中回忆起事实信息，而在其他语言中却无法做到。虽然这通常被视为一个需要缓解的问题，但在本工作中，我们提出将这种跨语言不一致性作为混合专家大语言模型可解释性的一种工具加以利用。我们的知识定位框架通过对比模型在正确回忆信息的语言集合与无法回忆的语言集合之间的路由行为，从而分离出在回答某项知识时发挥功能性作用的模型组件。我们的方法分为两个阶段：(1) 使用跨多种语言的困难事实问题查询模型，以生成“成功”和“失败”激活桶；(2) 对MoE路由器的逻辑值应用统计对比分析，以识别对知识重要的专家。为了验证必
tldr: 该论文提出将大语言模型的跨语言不一致性作为可解释性工具，通过对比模型在不同语言中事实回忆成功与失败时的MoE路由行为，定位混合专家模型中负责特定知识的关键专家。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes leveraging cross-lingual inconsistency in LLMs as an interpretability tool, contrasting MoE routing between languages where the model succeeds and fails at factual recall to localize experts responsible for specific knowledge.
